nina: Quick heads-up 1 opened a tiny PR to clarify the OpenAPI param for the generate endpoint. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1402

chao: What's the clarification about?

nina: The OpenAPI currently defines `context` as part of the request body, but in practice we accept it either as a JSON body field or as `X-Context` header for streaming callers. That ambiguity caused the JS streaming examples to show it in the body, while the curl examples used a header.

harper: Ah yeah, streaming clients often need headers. What's the proposed change?

nina: PR adds a components/parameters entry for `X-Context` and documents the header as the recommended surface for streaming and priority routing. It keeps `context` in the body for backward compatibility but marks the body field as "deprecated in docs" with a migration note. Also added `x-sdk-alias: context` so SDKs can map `context` -> header.

chao: Can you add a short example showing both forms and a note: "Prefer header for streaming; body accepted for legacy clients"? That will reduce confusion.

nina: Done. Example snippet in PR:

Curl (preferred):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \\n  -H "X-Context: user:42;session:abc" \\n  -d '{"input":"summarize this"}'
```

Legacy body form (still supported):
```
{
  "context": "user:42;session:abc",
  "input": "summarize this"
}
```

harper: Nice—small ask: add a one-line note in the OpenAPI parameter saying headers take precedence if both provided.

nina: Added that and a migration bullet: "If you previously sent context in the request body, switch to X-Context header for streaming and routing guarantees. SDKs accept `context` parameter and will set the header automatically."

chao: LGTM. docs-bot: Deploy preview: https://deploy-preview.docs.redwood.ai/1402

harper: I'll update the streaming examples and tests that asserted body-only presence.

nina: Thanks all, merging once CI passes. :shipit:
